purpose: Verify the integrity and arithmetic of 100 individually priced independent software IP assets. The new TA-IP-099 and TA-IP-100 have source-bound present-scope assessments; 98 preceding records retain their dates and prices. Website repositories remain excluded digital displays.

verification.browserIntegrity: The public renderer fetches the valuation register and methodology as raw text, recomputes SHA-256 in the browser and compares the result with this attestation.
verification.valuationReconciliation: The public renderer assembles the current asset register, applies published overrides, recalculates asset-level analytical economics and compares aggregate values with the published portfolio totals.
verification.publicSiteDirectory: The public project-site enhancer recomputes the SHA-256 digest of the site directory before presenting its integrity state.
verification.existenceBoundary: The timestamped public publication and matching digests demonstrate existence and integrity of the public commercial record as published. They do not independently prove authorship, legal title, patent priority, source-code identity, scientific validity, security assurance, certified valuation or commercial outcome.
verification.futureEconomicReferences: Verify the current 100-asset register. Numeric maturity sensitivities require each asset’s own established monetary baseline.
verification.sellerReadiness: Verify the dated criteria disclosure and corrected readiness records. Integrity checks establish unchanged published bytes and cross-register consistency; they do not establish completed transfer gates or independent certification.
verification.rightsTransfer: The public renderer verifies the seller-readiness, IP-ownership, software supply-chain, portfolio audit and rights-transfer records. The public transaction layer focuses on the offered rights, third-party obligations and transfer perimeter rather than internal development methods.
verification.projectEvaluations: Each of the 100 IP assets has its own evaluation, rights boundary and transfer perimeter. The two new software assets have dated source-content reviews and bounded local validation; all 98 preceding asset assessments and their evidence dates are retained.
verification.projectIdentities: Confirm unique TA-IP-001 through TA-IP-100 identifiers against the same project title, single reference alias and slug in every current register and digital-display entry.
verification.projectConnections: Verify the proposed-connection register, resolve every member against its independent TA-IP asset record, reject project reuse across combinations and recompute both the combined asking reference and recreation-cost total from the current individual financial references. This verifies identities, unique allocation and arithmetic; it does not establish technical integration.

privacyBoundary: Public records expose seller-side commercial, rights, transfer, evidence and non-sensitive supply-chain metadata only. Internal development methods, proprietary know-how, credentials, customer data, sensitive implementation details and transaction-confidential material remain outside the public showroom.

latestPageRefresh.boundary: All 97 default-branch heads and all 29 open pull requests were checked. Changed source, retained exact-code validation and bounded development scope were reviewed. latestFinancialReassessment.boundary: Two newly listed software repositories were reviewed and added as TA-IP-099 and TA-IP-100. All 29 LCTEP files and 56 selected SCEP files were checked against Git blob identities; the full SCEP tree contains 200 files, including historical material that was not executed. Fresh local checks passed 18 LCTEP tests and 14 SCEP tests without failures, errors or skips, syntax compilation and bounded CLI examples. All seven retained SCEP final-campaign files passed byte-length, SHA-256 and archive-integrity checks; four recorded source-file blobs match the current source. The retained 400-agent, 1000-step GPU campaign was not rerun. One step-50 checkpoint metadata file and seven binary parts are present. The metadata file was byte-verified; the binary parts were inventoried, not downloaded or restored. The overall checkpoint-part manifest and complete intermediate checkpoint set are not established, and a checkpoint checksum field contains a filename. Validation concerns bounded software execution and retained evidence, not flight qualification, consciousness, historical-output equivalence or independent certification. All 98 existing asset records, source dates, prices and readiness criteria are retained. Website repositories remain excluded digital displays.
